For analysts using the underlying microdata, the OECD Reader’s Companion should be consulted to identify the correct survey weights and any replicate-weight approach used for variance estimation.

data.outcome_summary: The OECD Survey of Adult Skills 2023 country note for Portugal reports adults’ proficiency in three domains—literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving—assessed in 2022–23 among adults aged 16–65 using a personal interview plus a self-completed digital assessment on tablets. Portugal participated for the first time in this cycle, enabling comparisons with OECD averages and selected comparison countries/economies. In Portugal, mean performance is below the OECD average in all three domains (literacy: 235; numeracy: 238; adaptive problem solving: 233), and large shares of adults are at low proficiency (e.g., 42% at Level 1 or below in literacy; 40% in numeracy; 42% in adaptive problem solving). The note also documents skill gaps by age and educational attainment and links higher numeracy proficiency to better employment outcomes and higher numeracy to higher wages (one standard-deviation increase in numeracy associated with 9% higher wages). Uncertainty is communicated via 95% confidence intervals, but the note does not provide the technical details needed to extract PV handling, missing-data procedures, or any ML model performance metrics.

The document does, however, provide key assessment design information (digital tablet administration, three domains, proficiency levels, and sample size/response rate) that supports interpretation of the reported proficiency benchmarks.
